Q: This is the adjuster calling about the auto claim you reported. Is it all right to record this statement?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give my first name for now, if that's okay.
Q: That's acceptable. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving thruogh Pasadena, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. Traffic was slow. A vehicle coming the
other way drifted into my lane and we ended up nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, more of a bump, but both frnot ends
were involved.
Q: What speed were you traveling when the vehicles made contact?
A: I'd guess maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. I had already slowed down because of the traffic ahead.
Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, they didn't. My car didn't go into any kind of crash mode.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene, and were you able to drive it away?
A: I got out and checked on the other driver. The car was drivable, but I had it towed because the front bumper was
pushed in and the hood wouldn't close right.
Q: How are you feeling physically since the collision?
A: My neck is stiff and sore, and it hurts when I turn my head to check my blind spot. Over the last few days I've also
had hedaaches that start at the base of my skull.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider about these symptoms?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They diagnosed wihplash and gave me a referral for physical
therapy.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add before we finish?
A: Only that I want to make sure the repair estimate reflects the damage to the front end, because it still doesn't feel
right when I brake.
Q: Thank you. I'll follow up with you about the next steps.
A: Thanks, I appreciate it.
